# Summary replay and delivery: source and operation-count investigation

Runtime core: c2bc5e78dfdb13f95bda970c5f4e0c247acbac29; documentation HEAD a7eb02bf1744dd0b1a4c9a4864866c4073a8e169. Production code is unchanged. The primary16g campaign reaches/completes/accepts OWASP12/11/11, conductor4/3/3, thingsboard2/1/1, Stirling6/5/5. New microtests do not run the iteration driver.

## Pipeline and existing deduplication

1. `RunMethodAnalyzer.retainSummary` admits a raw delta. `published` intersects it with fixed demand (apart from run1/backwardZERO exceptions). `queuePublications` retains selected demand publications and appends transport packets. A method queue-empty barrier detaches/flushed packets.
2. `SummaryStorage.publish` locks its per-callee PublicationIndex. `addAll` merges exact current summary content; empty deltas cause no notification. The index uses the same FLOW-backed law as method summaries. The lock captures the subscribed runner list after insertion. The publisher posts a detached fresh batch to each subscriber.
3. A caller input enters `SubscriptionManager.subscribe`. `CalleeSubscriptions.admit` merges an exact (CallerRef, GroupKey) current input and returns an immutable fresh delta. No growth means no replay. CallerRef preserves caller key, original premise, caller layer, call instruction and stage. There is no callee-only deduplication across these scopes.
4. For the admitted delta, production `ProtocolSteps.Inline` executes replay. `PublicationIndex.candidates` first enumerates geometrically related premise members. It then decodes/materializes ALL current conclusion groups for EACH candidate premise. Only afterwards does `SubscriptionManager.applyMatch` invoke the exact `ops.satisfying` predicate for each expanded publication.
5. New summary delivery uses `onDelivery`: for EACH publication/member, `CalleeSubscriptions.candidates` finds all geometrically related inputs, snapshots their current cumulative Facts, then `applyMatch` filters and applies them. Matching is on the receiving runner, not on the publisher thread.
6. A successful match invokes the AP summary application and then the remaining call stages, including rules/cleaners/bind-back/aliases. Output store deduplication occurs after this work; deduplicated output does not imply that the preceding matching and call suffix were free.

Both sides' path tries omit marks. A FLOW input can only satisfy a FLOW premise (Summary.kt24–40), but candidate lookup can still expand concrete premises before that constant-time rejection. A TAINT input can satisfy a concrete mark premise only for selected runtime atoms, or a FLOW premise under the existing mark gate. Layers are not a reject key: NORMAL and DEMAND participate and the result joins the layers. A proposed index must not drop cross-layer matches.

## Exact constructed counts, not project cardinalities

`SummaryCandidateWorkloadTest` uses real `PublicationIndex(flowBacked=true)`, `CalleeSubscriptions` and `matches`. It creates K=32 concrete mark premises with equal input base/path. Each premise has M=16 different output bases, so tree packing cannot collapse the output groups. There are32 input subscriptions with distinct call references.

| Quantity | Measured microtest count |
|---|---:|
| Stored publications |512|
| Replay expanded candidate packets |16,384|
| Replay accepted matches |512|
| Delivery candidate packets |16,384|
| Delivery accepted matches |512|
| Distinct replay (immutable input, premise) predicates |1,024|

Current candidate cost is K²M, while accepted pairs are KM.31/32 of these candidate filters reject their concrete mark. The output expansion M happens before the rejection. Reusing the same exact predicate once per (input,premise) lowers the constructed filter count by M=16; it does not remove necessary output applications. Early mark-aware selection can avoid the K mark matrix too, provided it preserves abstract/canonical/must semantics.

A second test stores one premise and32 output groups. Every `matches` invocation has exactly the same input and premise and returns the same selected Facts. The32 output applications remain distinct, but32 applicability filters are unnecessary. This output multiplier also exists with a single mark. Real field outputs often pack into one tree, so neither K32 nor M16 is asserted for any measured project.

A third legal queued schedule registers an input, inserts a publication, delivers it, and then performs delayed replay. The applier is called twice for one logical pair. Existing protocol tests check the set of results for these orders, not an exactly-once application count. Production replay is Inline; another runner can still insert/notify between registration and the replay read. This proves possible duplicate work, not its project rate or a dominant multiplier.

All three tests pass after declaring their names in the frozen fixture namespace (`T0..T31`, `T`). The first attempt used undeclared arbitrary names and failed before reaching the measured operation. No production declaration policy was changed. See evidence.json and copied XML/log.

## Existing project counters

The following are END−START differences of additive N2 counters, not live retained sizes. AcceptedDeltas is a nonempty subscription admission. It normally enters a replay; an interrupted run may stop between those operations. New ordinary groups and zero-only entries are separate. Growth admissions are accepted − new groups − zero-only.

| Project / phase | Accepted delta admissions | New groups | Zero-only entries | Growth admissions | New path postings |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| conductor run4 (TIMEOUT) |5,875,334|812,423|33,562|5,029,349|7,642,936|
| thingsboard run2 (TIMEOUT) |3,583,037|1,463,374|207,927|1,911,736|2,753,817|
| Stirling run5 (COMPLETE) |1,662,369|1,217,561|0|444,808|1,510,967|

OWASP backward8→10 has exactly the same admission/group/posting totals, while outgoing demand grows772,627→2,543,694 and engine time88.705→304.586s. More N2 input admissions do not explain that growth. More work inside each admission, larger published relations/trees, and demand construction remain candidates. Those effects are not separated by the current counters.

The saved N2 interface has no general summary replay/delivery candidate, exact-match, reject, decoded-output or applied-summary counters. Its `replayCandidates` names belong to the separate run1 mark-request join, not ordinary summaries. `queuedReplays` includes an executing Inline callback; the shared peak10 does not mean a ten-item persistent queue per method or per phase. Current directory gauges are zero after release and cannot give a peak retained census. Current E6 counts are zero in conductor run4 and the backward phases; Stirling run5 has only30 new E6 combinations. Do not attribute these millions of unary admissions to ND products.

## Source-confirmed repeated search

`DiagonalRelations.borrow` computes one canonical abstract initial for the requested concrete initial. It then visits EVERY `headers` scope and tests `scope.initial !== flow` before visiting rows. Each scope includes (initial, output base, layer). The exact initial identity is already known, so all scopes for other initials are irrelevant to this query. The current storage can contain many output bases/layers/initials. The issue is repeated unrelated search, not merely slower equality.

The saved conductor run4 late30 window has `DiagonalRelations$borrow$1.invokeSuspend` as a Java leaf in28.23% of634 samples. Its path is subscribe→replay→SummaryStorage candidates→PublicationIndex publications→DiagonalRelations borrow. The middle30 has onDelivery in176/177 stacks, but some of that may be nested Inline replay or call-suffix work. Inclusive onDelivery is not a count of time spent in its candidate loop. A fresh narrow reader is being prepared to separate those nested paths. No sample percentage is an operation count or fixed speedup.

## Work avoidance candidates and proof scope

### A. Match a premise before expanding its conclusions

Current replay:

```text
for each geometrically related premise member:
    decode all current output groups
    for each output group:
        selected = satisfying(freshInput, premise)
        if selected != null: apply selected + output
```

Candidate design:

```text
for each geometrically related premise member:
    selected = satisfying(freshInput, premise)
    if selected == null: continue
    for each current output group:
        apply selected + output
```

This changes neither the exact predicate nor any output transfer. Its key is the exact immutable input snapshot, canonical member premise and mode, including record=false and zero-only rules. Keep tail/E/mx/protection. The current `matches` depends on no conclusion field. This is a query-local value, not a permanent join cache or additional history. Replay must preserve the existing linearizable snapshot requirement; doing the pure predicate in the existing storage read lock is a simple reference design, with lock-duration effects to measure.

### B. Share delivery selection for equal premise/member batches

Current delivery rebuilds candidate snapshots and selected Facts for every output group. Grouping equal full premise/member publications could perform those steps once. However, callback effects can add inputs between publications. The old code snapshots once per publication; a group snapshot changes timing. That is a required protocol proof, not a silent implementation detail.

For inputs present at the group snapshot, every selected output still applies. A later input has its own registered fresh replay; because the whole notification batch was inserted before delivery, that replay sees all current outputs. Current FLOW replacement may have removed an older marked packet, so this proof must use the existing coverage/subsumption preservation law, including protected output and alias closure. Preserve full ND keys, layers, contexts, stage, source/sink observations and cancellation accounting. Do not simply mark a callee/premise 'already answered' after one match.

### C. Avoid unrelated diagonal scopes

Partition or index the existing current scope directory by canonical abstract initial. Preserve all current base/layer/tail/E/geometry/mask/protection cells and removal/compaction semantics. This is an index change with equality of borrowed results to prove. It removes the known all-scope search. Its project impact depends on query count, total scopes and matching scopes, not only leaf sample share.

## Bounded project diagnostics still needed

Per runner/store primitive counters should count replay queries, geometric premise members, output groups expanded, exact match calls/successes, delivery publication/member groups, candidate inputs snapshotted, and applications. Diagonal lookup should count total scopes visited and exact-initial scopes accepted. Track a small top-method/call sample or fixed histograms for output fanout M, without retaining the pair product or whole Facts histories. Count downstream fresh output admissions separately from AP application success.

Project reject rates, repeated equal-predicate fanout and duplicate replay/delivery pair rates are not present in current logs. A full-pair seen set would recreate the memory problem and should not be added for this investigation. Use a bounded exact sample for the overlap question, and record omissions. No production optimization or new project campaign was run for these notes.

# Demand handling: source and work evidence

Date: 29 October 2026. Repo HEAD: a7eb02bf1. Runtime core: 3284369b2.
No production source was changed. This reader did not run a project analyzer,
profile reader or heap tool. The parent ran the new small tests in the combined
targeted Gradle test job. All nine selected tests passed.

A later external counter patch adds graph diagnostics only in
`/drive-testcomp/opentaint-go-rules/summary-demand-counters-20261029/worktree`.
Its separate `preparation/graph-counter-binding.json` records source hashes,
metric IDs and preservation checks. It changes no main production source.

Latest primary progress is unchanged: OWASP reached run-12, completed and accepted
run-11; conductor reached run-4, completed and accepted run-3; thingsboard reached
run-2, completed and accepted run-1; Stirling reached run-6, completed and accepted
run-5. All 16g primary runs stopped on timeout.

## 1. What the counters prove

`c2Direct` counts calls to `DemandStore.initials`, not matched rows or new facts.
`restrictedIntersections` counts the initial keys returned by these queries at
`RunMethodAnalyzer.addLink`. `initialCandidates` counts all `addInitial` calls.
The last counter also includes direct backward ZERO entry and run-1 answer work.
`newInitials` counts all newly admitted initial keys.

In the four phases below, `c2Direct` equals processed LinkIn calls (`inputArrivals`).
This equality is observed, not a general API rule: the limit callback can emit
more than one bounded packet before C2 runs.

| 16g phase | C2 calls | C2 returned initial keys | All fresh initials | C5 restrict calls | C5 graph states |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| conductor run-4 | 10,254,004 | 5,023,432 | 201,266 | 5,499,548 | 0 |
| thingsboard run-2 | 3,048,127 | 2,239,680 | 616,342 | 5,139,321 | 4,923,059 |
| Stirling run-5 | 2,065,402 | 1,796,375 | 466,826 | 1,114,634 | 0 |
| Stirling run-6 | 1,127,763 | 705,412 | 146,795 | 562,671 | 0 |

A C2 call that creates an initial contributes at least one fresh initial. Thus
`C2 calls - all fresh initials` is a lower bound on calls with no new admission.
It gives 98.04%, 79.78%, 77.40% and 86.98% for the four rows above. These are calls
observed through cancellation, not a claim that every call completed normally.
They are not a claim that every such call can be skipped.

Similarly, at least 4,822,166 conductor C2 answers repeat a held initial key:
`C2 returned keys - all fresh initials`. This is 95.99% of its C2 answers. Direct
ZERO work is included in the fresh upper bound, so the subtraction is conservative.
Do not call the duplicate fraction of all initialCandidates a C2 duplicate-query
fraction.

## 2. A measured avoidable link path

The only production link call is in `RunMethodCallServices.enterCallees`:

```kotlin
subscribe(Subscription(callee, ref, facts.layer, facts))
link(callee, ref, facts.layer, facts)
```

The subscription is admitted synchronously on the caller's runner. It can reject
the complete input as unchanged. The return type is Unit, so the following link
still sends the full input. `addLink` then performs limit/admission work in the
callee. N2 already retains the current input for future summary application.

Let Q be processed LinkIn calls and A be all accepted N2 deltas. Every processed
link has one earlier subscription call. Each accepted linked subscription adds
one to A. A also includes zeroOnly subscriptions and subscriptions whose later
link was still queued or interrupted. Thus `max(0,Q-A)` is a lower bound on links
whose matching caller subscription admitted no delta.

| 16g phase | Processed links Q | All N2 accepted deltas A | Rejected-subscription links at least |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| conductor run-4 | 10,254,004 | 5,875,334 | 4,378,670 (42.70%) |
| thingsboard run-2 | 3,048,127 | 3,583,037 | 0; no useful lower bound |
| Stirling run-5 | 2,065,402 | 1,662,369 | 403,033 (19.51%) |
| Stirling run-6 | 1,127,763 | 744,864 | 382,899 (33.95%) |

Same-run reentrant replay does not break the pairing. A rejected subscription
starts no replay; an accepted subscription can add work before its own link, but
that only increases the conservative A bound. The first accepted DEMAND link must
still arrive before a complete barrier. Skipping a later duplicate cannot erase
that input-presence contribution in a complete run.

This is a work-removal candidate: keep caller input admission and replay, then
send a callee link only for the admitted fresh delta. For restricted runs, C2 is
a set union of independent scalar emissions over a fixed demand snapshot. Exact
same-header accumulation is an ordinary leaf union. Limit is also a per-leaf
map/union, split by kept/cut header. These are the needed local identities; they
must be proved and tested across tails, exclusions, packed marks, protection-only
growth and run-2 static completion before implementation. The run-1 request/static
protocol is a separate obligation. No fix is made here.

## 3. C5 loses the association already found by its index

Local C5 does this:

```text
for each output leaf: add related exit row IDs to one shared set
for each original member:
    for each entry-prefix row ID:
        if ID is in that output set:
            restrict(the whole raw packet, this paired row)
```

`restrictRaw` then enumerates every scalar raw leaf again for every selected pair.
`insideDemand(original, entry)` is also tested inside that leaf loop. If a TAINT
packet has a protection mask, `transportProtection` repeats the operation for the
protected and ordinary packet. Only after restriction does result collection
deduplicate equal outputs and join their protection.

Use this small code shape:

```java
Box fanout(Object p, int choice) {
    Box r = new Box();
    switch (choice) {
        case 0: r.f0 = p; break;
        case 1: r.f1 = p; break;
        // K disjoint alternatives
    }
    return r;
}
```

```text
Original: p.* / FLOW
Raw packet: {ret.f0.*, ..., ret.fK-1.*} / FLOW, NORMAL
Demand: K paired rows, each (entry=p.*, exit=ret.fi.*)

Output trie: K relevant leaf/row associations
Current whole-packet route: K restrict calls, each scans K leaves
Scalar reference: K*K cells, K nonempty outputs
Leaf-associated route: K relevant scalar cells, same K outputs
```

`DemandCandidateWorkloadTest` checks the actual production result at widths 1,
4, 16 and 64, and the production c5Restrict counter K. It separately counts the
full reference's K*K scalar attempts and the exit trie's K relevant pairs. It does
not pretend that the public production counter measures inner scalar tests. The
production K*K behavior follows from the source loops for this valid packet.
The protected variant checks that the same K output memberships remain protected.

A future indexed scalar join could retain each output-leaf/exit-row association
and restrict only those cells. It must still use the complete paired entry/exit
row, all ND members, current reference tail/E rules and the exact protection mask.
It cannot replace a pair with independent entry and exit sets. The real-project
raw packet width and the number of rejected inner cells are not logged yet.

## 4. Run-2 C5 offers intermediate states that cannot match the raw output

`StaticPairLookup.walk` uses the raw outputs only for an initial endpoint-existence
test. It then sends every BFS state to `offer`, even if the state's left endpoint
has a different base from the provided raw packet. A restriction against a wrong
base cannot return a result. It still enumerates the raw leaves, and may transport
protection first.

```text
Raw output base: argument0
State: C.f -> ret
Current: restrict raw argument0 packet against exit C.f; reject every leaf
Required: keep traversing C.f predecessors, but do not restrict this state
```

Thingsboard has 4,923,059 graph states and 5,139,321 restriction calls. Their ratio
is 95.8%, but that is not a rejection rate or a CPU fraction. We do not yet know
how many raw outputs are static, or how many states fail this base check.

A stronger pruning candidate uses the fixed right endpoint. Left composition
does not change its geometry. Once a state is mapped, its right output mark is
fixed too. If it cannot contain the current original premise, more left
composition cannot repair it. Pruning must keep a FLOW prefix until a later
mapped prefix fixes the output mark. It must not reject a state merely because
the intermediate static input has the wrong mark.

## 5. C2 repeats a fixed abstract answer

For an abstract entry, `emit(entry,actual)` returns `flowForm(entry)` after a
location-overlap test. The answer does not depend on the actual concrete mark.
The current query scalarizes every actual mark, visits entries, calls emit, and
then deduplicates initial keys. The method's InitialFactStore deduplicates again
after the query.

```text
Fixed demand entry: argument0.* / FLOW
Arrival 1: argument0 / T -> initial argument0.* / FLOW (new)
Arrival 2: argument0 / U -> initial argument0.* / FLOW (already held)
```

The new C2 test checks this exact repeated canonical answer with production
DemandStore and InitialFactStore. A run-local admission view could retire that
fixed abstract answer after the first admission. Concrete entries need a separate
rule because their emitted path/tail/E can vary with the actual input. Neither
all initial-duplicate counts nor the current source prove that most real-project
repeats are abstract. This needs one additional split before ranking the change.

## 6. Required bounded diagnostic splits

A fresh narrow reader of the current thingsboard run-2 recording changes the
priority. Of 38,206 Java execution samples, C2 is inclusive in 11,267 (29.49%), C5
in 18,008 (47.13%) and StaticPairLookup.walk in 17,965 (47.02%). restrictRaw is
inclusive in only 87 (0.23%). These selectors overlap. They are not wall-time or
native CPU shares. The local K*K restriction case is real, but it is not the
dominant sampled cost in this thingsboard phase. Removing scalar restriction
calls alone cannot be presented as the main fix for that phase.

C2's leaves include Reachability.reachesAny in 3,589 samples, HashMap.putVal in
2,571 and HashMap.resize in 1,817. FrozenStaticCompletion creates a new View for
every local/visible query. Each visible View has its own lazy Reachability scratch
for the same fixed method and graph. A graph vertex is expanded at most once per
lookup, but repeated lookups can repeat the same call-graph tour. The source and
samples identify a concrete reuse opportunity across queries, rather than making
each HashMap operation faster. A mutable View cache inside the shared immutable
DemandStore would violate the current ownership/thread-safety contract. A future
design must choose an actor-owned query context or a compact immutable eligibility
index, and measure its memory bound. No such cache or index is added here.

C5's leaves include MarkTable.isGroup, list suffix/equality work and overlap under
the graph walk. This supports the fixed-endpoint subtree investigation above,
not a claim that all 4.9 million states are irrelevant.

The present counters show outer calls, not inner work. The next isolated
diagnostic should add numeric counters at existing loops, not a retained edge log:

* Subscription admission: accepted, rejected and delta-only growth, split by
  zeroOnly and restricted/run-1 mode. Count each link after that exact decision.
* C2: scalar actual leaves; abstract and concrete entry visits; no-match entries;
  returned keys fresh/already held; calls with no fresh key; abstract fixed keys
  already admitted. Do not store every input packet to get these counts.
* C5 local: exit index postings visited, unioned row IDs, raw scalar leaves scanned
  per selected row, initial/mark/base/path rejection reasons, emitted cells, and
  ordinary versus protection pass work.
* C5 graph: states rejected by fixed right-endpoint geometry/mark, intermediate
  left-base/path rejects, states that still need traversal, and actual successful
  restrictions. Keep logical state and restriction counts separate.
* Call-graph eligibility: new reachability scratch objects, unique method roots,
  owner-family pairs, expanded vertices/edges and repeated eligibility results.
  This split is required before selecting a cache shape or retention budget.
* Protection: exact ordinary repeat versus newly grown protected mask. Facts
  equality omits the mask; a cache keyed only by Facts equality is incomplete.

Sample exact repeated complete-query keys only in a bounded diagnostic window.
The key must include the demand snapshot/method, original premise, ordinary
Facts header/tree, raw layer and full protection mask. A C2 key can omit protection
because admission does not use it, but must retain tails, field/mark exclusions,
mark-group compatibility and current field limit. Input links and caller replay
effects cannot be skipped just because C2 returns no new initial.

## Evidence

`counters-and-source.json` contains both saved 8/12g and current 16g phase counters,

this investigation is `DemandCandidateWorkloadTest.kt`. No expected whole-project

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read complete counter END lines. This tool does not inspect live JVM state."""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import math
import pathlib
import re


ROOT = pathlib.Path('/drive-testcomp/opentaint-go-rules/summary-demand-counters-20261029')
PAIRS = re.compile(r'([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=(-?\d+)')
HISTOGRAMS = {
    'C2_ACTUAL_LEAVES_': ('C2_QUERIES', 'C2_ACTUAL_LEAVES'),
    'C2_RETURNED_KEYS_': ('C2_QUERIES', 'C2_RETURNED_KEYS'),
    'C5_RAW_LEAVES_': ('C5_QUERIES', 'C5_RAW_LEAVES'),
    'C5_PAIR_OFFERS_': ('C5_QUERIES', 'C5_PAIR_OFFERS'),
}
REASONS = ['C5_REJECT_INITIAL_GEOMETRY', 'C5_REJECT_INITIAL_MARK',
           'C5_REJECT_TARGET_MARK', 'C5_REJECT_TARGET_BASE',
           'C5_REJECT_TARGET_GEOMETRY', 'C5_REJECT_NO_EXIT', 'C5_SCALAR_ACCEPTED']


def ratio(a, b):
    return a / b if b else None


def histogram(metrics, prefix):
    rows = []
    for i in range(20):
        low = 0 if i == 0 else 1 << (i - 1)
        high = 0 if i == 0 else (None if i == 19 else (1 << i) - 1)
        suffix = '0' if i == 0 else ('262144plus' if i == 19 else '%dto%d' % (low, high))
        rows.append({'name': prefix + suffix, 'low': low, 'high': high,
                     'count': metrics.get(prefix + suffix, 0)})
    samples = sum(x['count'] for x in rows)
    low_sum = sum(x['low'] * x['count'] for x in rows)
    high_sum = None if rows[-1]['count'] else sum(x['high'] * x['count'] for x in rows[:-1])
    quantiles = {}
    for q in (0.5, 0.9, 0.99):
        rank = math.ceil(q * samples)
        total = 0
        selected = None
        for row in rows:
            total += row['count']
            if samples and total >= rank:
                selected = {'low': row['low'], 'high': row['high']}
                break
        quantiles[str(q)] = selected
    return {'samples': samples, 'weighted_total_low': low_sum,
            'weighted_total_high': high_sum, 'quantile_buckets': quantiles, 'buckets': rows}


def derive(metrics, status, graph_vertices=None, graph_edges=None):
    n = lambda key: metrics.get(key, 0)
    complete = status == 'COMPLETE'
    checks = []

    def equality(label, started, outcomes):
        gap = started - outcomes
        checks.append({'name': label, 'started': started, 'outcomes': outcomes, 'gap': gap,
                       'result': 'PASS' if gap == 0 else
                       ('GAP_ALLOWED_IN_PARTIAL_RUN' if not complete and gap > 0 else 'REVIEW')})

    equality('C2 scalar emit sources', n('C2_EMIT_CHECKS'),
             n('C2_ENTRY_OFFERS') - n('C2_OFFER_DUPLICATES') + n('C2_HAS_CHECKS') + n('C2_REQUIRE_CHECKS'))
    equality('C5 pair-offer sources', n('C5_PAIR_OFFERS'), sum(n(k) for k in
             ('C5_LOCAL_OFFERS', 'C5_PRIMITIVE_OFFERS', 'C5_LOCAL_BFS_OFFERS', 'C5_VISIBLE_BFS_OFFERS')))
    equality('C5 exit-bearing pair offers', n('C5_PAIR_OFFERS'), n('C5_RESTRICT_CALLS') + n('C5_NO_EXIT'))
    equality('C5 scalar pass partition', n('C5_SCALAR_RESTRICT'),
             n('C5_SCALAR_ORDINARY') + n('C5_SCALAR_PROTECTED'))
    equality('C5 scalar terminal branch partition', n('C5_SCALAR_RESTRICT'), sum(n(k) for k in REASONS))
    equality('C5 BFS admission partition', n('C5_BFS_STATES_ATTEMPTED'),
             n('C5_BFS_STATES_ADMITTED') + n('C5_BFS_STATES_DUPLICATE'))
    equality('C5 popped-state offers', n('C5_BFS_STATES_POPPED'),
             n('C5_LOCAL_BFS_OFFERS') + n('C5_VISIBLE_BFS_OFFERS'))
    equality('Graph scratch-root classification', n('CG_SCRATCH_CREATED'),
             n('CG_UNIQUE_ROOTS_GRAPH_LIFETIME') + n('CG_REPEATED_ROOT_SCRATCH') + n('CG_UNKNOWN_ROOT_SCRATCH'))
    equality('Graph reachesAny outcomes', n('CG_REACHES_ANY_CALLS'),
             n('CG_ENTRY_SEEN_HITS') + n('CG_TRAVERSAL_HITS') + n('CG_EXHAUSTED_CALLS'))
    equality('Graph owner searches per examined edge', n('CG_EDGES_EXAMINED'), n('CG_OWNER_SEARCHES'))
    equality('Graph discovered-vertex accounting', n('CG_NEW_VERTICES'),
             n('CG_SCRATCH_CREATED') - n('CG_UNKNOWN_ROOT_SCRATCH') +
             n('CG_EDGES_EXAMINED') - n('CG_SEEN_EDGES'))
    for kind in ('LOCAL', 'VISIBLE'):
        equality('Graph %s view classification' % kind, n('CG_%s_VIEWS' % kind),
                 sum(n('CG_%s_%s_VIEWS' % (scope, kind)) for scope in ('C2', 'C5', 'OTHER')))
    hists = {}
    for prefix, (queries, total) in HISTOGRAMS.items():
        h = histogram(metrics, prefix)
        h.update({'query_calls': n(queries), 'query_calls_without_histogram': n(queries) - h['samples'],
                  'measured_total': n(total), 'mean_on_histogrammed_calls': ratio(n(total), h['samples'])})
        h['total_in_bucket_range'] = (h['weighted_total_low'] <= n(total) and
                                     (h['weighted_total_high'] is None or n(total) <= h['weighted_total_high']))
        hists[prefix] = h
        equality(prefix + ' sample calls', n(queries), h['samples'])
    fixed_bad = n('C5_BFS_ENTRY_GEOMETRY_BAD') + n('C5_BFS_FIXED_MAPPED_OUTPUT_MARK_BAD')
    cg = {'views': {k: v for k, v in metrics.items() if k.startswith('CG_') and 'VIEW' in k},
          'scratch_created': n('CG_SCRATCH_CREATED'),
          'new_graph_root_ids': n('CG_UNIQUE_ROOTS_GRAPH_LIFETIME'),
          'repeated_root_scratch': n('CG_REPEATED_ROOT_SCRATCH'),
          'repeated_root_scratch_fraction': ratio(n('CG_REPEATED_ROOT_SCRATCH'),
                                                n('CG_SCRATCH_CREATED') - n('CG_UNKNOWN_ROOT_SCRATCH')),
          'reaches_any_calls': n('CG_REACHES_ANY_CALLS'),
          'vertices_expanded': n('CG_VERTICES_EXPANDED'), 'edges_examined': n('CG_EDGES_EXAMINED'),
          'vertices_per_scratch': ratio(n('CG_VERTICES_EXPANDED'), n('CG_SCRATCH_CREATED')),
          'edges_per_scratch': ratio(n('CG_EDGES_EXAMINED'), n('CG_SCRATCH_CREATED')),
          'entry_seen_hit_fraction': ratio(n('CG_ENTRY_SEEN_HITS'), n('CG_REACHES_ANY_CALLS')),
          'empty_owner_calls': n('CG_EMPTY_OWNER_CALLS'),
          'empty_owner_call_fraction': ratio(n('CG_EMPTY_OWNER_CALLS'), n('CG_REACHES_ANY_CALLS')),
          'frozen_graph_vertices': graph_vertices, 'frozen_graph_edges': graph_edges,
          'vertex_scan_volume_in_V_units': ratio(n('CG_VERTICES_EXPANDED'), graph_vertices),
          'edge_scan_volume_in_E_units': ratio(n('CG_EDGES_EXAMINED'), graph_edges),
          'root_tour_repeats_lower_bound_single_graph':
              max(0, math.ceil(n('CG_VERTICES_EXPANDED') / graph_vertices) - graph_vertices)
              if graph_vertices else None,
          'limits': ['Repeated-root scratch can return on an own-root seen hit with no graph expansion.',
                     'Unique roots are graph-instance/root-ID pairs over each graph lifetime.',
                     'The tour lower bound assumes one frozen graph with the stated V; it is deliberately weak.',
                     'Scan-volume ratios are units of work, not a count of full traversal invocations.']}
    return {'validation_mode': 'COMPLETE_EXPECT_BALANCE' if complete else 'PARTIAL_ALLOW_GAPS',
            'checks': checks, 'histograms': hists,
            'C2': {'entry_offers': n('C2_ENTRY_OFFERS'),
                   'within_query_duplicate_offers': n('C2_OFFER_DUPLICATES'),
                   'within_query_duplicate_offer_fraction': ratio(n('C2_OFFER_DUPLICATES'), n('C2_ENTRY_OFFERS')),
                   'emit_checks': n('C2_EMIT_CHECKS'), 'emit_reject_fraction': ratio(n('C2_EMIT_REJECTS'), n('C2_EMIT_CHECKS')),
                   'returned_keys': n('C2_RETURNED_KEYS'),
                   'note': 'Emit checks include offer, has and requireFamily. These are not cross-query cache hits or new admissions.'},
            'C5': {'pair_offer_sources': {k: n(k) for k in ('C5_LOCAL_OFFERS', 'C5_PRIMITIVE_OFFERS',
                                                          'C5_LOCAL_BFS_OFFERS', 'C5_VISIBLE_BFS_OFFERS')},
                   'scalar_reason_counts': {k: n(k) for k in REASONS},
                   'scalar_reason_fractions': {k: ratio(n(k), n('C5_SCALAR_RESTRICT')) for k in REASONS},
                   'scalar_attempts_per_restrict_call': ratio(n('C5_SCALAR_RESTRICT'), n('C5_RESTRICT_CALLS')),
                   'protection_passes_per_restrict_call': ratio(n('C5_PROTECTION_PASSES'), n('C5_RESTRICT_CALLS')),
                   'bfs_fixed_entry_bad_pops': fixed_bad,
                   'bfs_fixed_entry_bad_pop_fraction': ratio(fixed_bad, n('C5_BFS_STATES_POPPED')),
                   'bfs_static_bridges_after_fixed_entry_reject': n('C5_BFS_BRIDGES_AFTER_FIXED_ENTRY_REJECT'),
                   'bfs_static_bridges_after_fixed_entry_reject_fraction':
                       ratio(n('C5_BFS_BRIDGES_AFTER_FIXED_ENTRY_REJECT'), n('C5_BFS_STATIC_BRIDGES')),
                   'bfs_current_output_mismatch': n('C5_BFS_OUTPUT_MISMATCH'),
                   'bfs_output_mismatch_static_bridges': n('C5_BFS_OUTPUT_MISMATCH_STATIC_BRIDGES'),
                   'bfs_admitted_not_popped': n('C5_BFS_STATES_ADMITTED') - n('C5_BFS_STATES_POPPED'),
                   'note': 'Current output mismatch can still need bridge traversal. Admitted-not-popped also includes safe coverage stops.'},
            'graph': cg}


def parse_log(data):
    newline = data.rfind(b'\n')
    prefix = data[:newline + 1] if newline >= 0 else b''
    text = prefix.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    phases = {}
    analysis_end = None
    graph = {}
    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        match = re.search(r'BIDI_RUN_START run=(\d+) direction=(\w+) limit=(\d+)', line)
        if match:
            run = int(match[1])
            phases.setdefault(run, {}).update(run=run, direction=match[2], field_limit=int(match[3]), start_line=number)
        match = re.search(r'BIDI_RUN_END run=(\d+) status=(\w+)', line)
        if match:
            run = int(match[1]); phases.setdefault(run, {}).update(run=run, engine_status=match[2], engine_end_line=number)
        match = re.search(r'BIDI_WORK_COUNTS run=(\d+) phase=(START|END)', line)
        if match:
            run = int(match[1]); row = phases.setdefault(run, {'run': run})
            metrics = {k: int(v) for k, v in PAIRS.findall(line) if k != 'run'}
            snapshot = {'line': number, 'status': re.search(r'\bstatus=(\w+)', line).group(1)
                        if re.search(r'\bstatus=(\w+)', line) else None,
                        'metrics': metrics, 'line_sha256': hashlib.sha256(line.encode()).hexdigest()}
            row.setdefault('counter_snapshots', {}).setdefault(match[2], []).append(snapshot)
        if 'BIDI_STATIC_CLOSURE_LOOKUP' in line or 'BIDI_STATIC_CLOSURE_HANDOFF' in line:
            fields = {k: int(v) for k, v in PAIRS.findall(line) if k != 'run'}
            if 'callMethods' in fields:
                graph = {'vertices': fields['callMethods'], 'edges': fields.get('callEdges'), 'line': number}
            match = re.search(r'\brun=(\d+)', line)
            if match and 'BIDI_STATIC_CLOSURE_LOOKUP' in line:
                phases.setdefault(int(match[1]), {'run': int(match[1])})['legacy_query_statistics'] = fields
        match = re.search(r'Run (\d+) \((FORWARD|BACKWARD)\) frontier: analysed (\d+), demand edges (\d+)', line)
        if match:
            phases.setdefault(int(match[1]), {'run': int(match[1])})['frontier'] = {
                'direction': match[2], 'analysed': int(match[3]), 'demand_edges': int(match[4]), 'line': number}
        match = re.search(r'BIDI_ANALYSIS_END run=(\d+) status=(\w+) reason=(\w+)', line)
        if match:
            analysis_end = {'run': int(match[1]), 'status': match[2], 'reason': match[3], 'line': number}
    for run, phase in phases.items():
        snapshots = phase.get('counter_snapshots', {}).get('END', [])
        if snapshots:
            final = snapshots[-1]
            phase['counter_status'] = final['status']
            phase['metrics'] = final['metrics']
            phase['duplicate_counter_END_lines'] = len(snapshots) - 1
            phase['derived'] = derive(final['metrics'], final['status'], graph.get('vertices'), graph.get('edges'))
            legacy = phase.get('legacy_query_statistics', {})
            phase['legacy_crosschecks'] = []
            for old, new in [('c2Direct', 'C2_QUERIES'), ('c5Candidates', 'C5_PAIR_OFFERS'),
                             ('c5Restrict', 'C5_RESTRICT_CALLS'), ('c5States', 'C5_BFS_STATES_ADMITTED'),
                             ('c2Visible', 'CG_C2_VISIBLE_VIEWS'), ('c5Visible', 'CG_C5_VISIBLE_VIEWS')]:
                if old in legacy:
                    actual = final['metrics'].get(new, 0)
                    phase['legacy_crosschecks'].append({'legacy': old, 'new': new,
                                                       'legacy_value': legacy[old], 'new_value': actual,
                                                       'result': 'PASS' if legacy[old] == actual else 'REVIEW'})
    return {'input_complete_prefix_bytes': len(prefix), 'input_complete_prefix_sha256': hashlib.sha256(prefix).hexdigest(),
            'ignored_unterminated_bytes': len(data) - len(prefix), 'phases': [phases[k] for k in sorted(phases)],
            'analysis_end': analysis_end, 'graph_metadata': graph,
            'progress': {'latest_reached': max((p['run'] for p in phases.values() if 'start_line' in p), default=None),
                         'latest_complete_engine': max((p['run'] for p in phases.values() if p.get('engine_status') == 'COMPLETE'), default=None),
                         'latest_accepted_forward_frontier': max((p['run'] for p in phases.values()
                                                                if p.get('frontier', {}).get('direction') == 'FORWARD'), default=None),
                         'latest_counter_END': max((p['run'] for p in phases.values() if 'metrics' in p), default=None)}}


def render(result):
    lines = ['# Summary/demand operation counts', '', 'Diagnostic only. These times are not a performance comparison.',
             '', 'As of: ' + result['as_of_utc'], '', 'Progress: ' + json.dumps(result['progress']), '']
    for p in result['phases']:
        lines += ['## run-%d (%s, limit %s)' % (p['run'], p.get('direction', '?'), p.get('field_limit', '?')), '']
        if 'metrics' not in p:
            lines += ['No complete counter END line yet.', '']; continue
        d = p['derived']; m = p['metrics']; n = lambda k: m.get(k, 0)
        lines += ['Counter status: ' + str(p['counter_status']), '',
                  '* C2 calls / actual leaves / returned keys: %s / %s / %s.' %
                  (n('C2_QUERIES'), n('C2_ACTUAL_LEAVES'), n('C2_RETURNED_KEYS')),
                  '* C2 entry offers / within-query duplicates / emit checks / emit rejects: %s / %s / %s / %s.' %
                  (n('C2_ENTRY_OFFERS'), n('C2_OFFER_DUPLICATES'), n('C2_EMIT_CHECKS'), n('C2_EMIT_REJECTS')),
                  '* C5 calls / pair offers / scalar attempts / accepted scalar cells: %s / %s / %s / %s.' %
                  (n('C5_QUERIES'), n('C5_PAIR_OFFERS'), n('C5_SCALAR_RESTRICT'), n('C5_SCALAR_ACCEPTED')),
                  '* C5 offer sources: ' + json.dumps(d['C5']['pair_offer_sources']),
                  '* C5 scalar reasons: ' + json.dumps(d['C5']['scalar_reason_counts']),
                  '* C5 fixed bad entry popped states / bridges after fixed reject: %s / %s.' %
                  (d['C5']['bfs_fixed_entry_bad_pops'], n('C5_BFS_BRIDGES_AFTER_FIXED_ENTRY_REJECT')),
                  '* C5 current-output mismatches / still-needed candidate bridges: %s / %s. These are not all prunable.' %
                  (n('C5_BFS_OUTPUT_MISMATCH'), n('C5_BFS_OUTPUT_MISMATCH_STATIC_BRIDGES')),
                  '* Graph scratches / new graph roots / repeated-root scratches: %s / %s / %s.' %
                  (n('CG_SCRATCH_CREATED'), n('CG_UNIQUE_ROOTS_GRAPH_LIFETIME'), n('CG_REPEATED_ROOT_SCRATCH')),
                  '* Graph expanded vertices / examined edges / empty-owner calls: %s / %s / %s.' %
                  (n('CG_VERTICES_EXPANDED'), n('CG_EDGES_EXAMINED'), n('CG_EMPTY_OWNER_CALLS')), '']
        for prefix, h in d['histograms'].items():
            nonempty = [(x['name'], x['count']) for x in h['buckets'] if x['count']]
            lines += [prefix + ': ' + json.dumps(nonempty), '']
        review = [c for c in d['checks'] if c['result'] != 'PASS']
        cross_review = [c for c in p['legacy_crosschecks'] if c['result'] != 'PASS']
        lines += ['Nonzero balance gaps: ' + json.dumps(review),
                  'Legacy/new counter discrepancies: ' + json.dumps(cross_review), '']
    lines += ['Repeated scratch roots do not prove every scratch traversed the graph. See measured vertex/edge totals.',
              'Partial calls can start without a terminal result. No equality is asserted for interrupted work.',
              'Raw counts are operations, not retained objects, scalar facts, wall time or CPU shares.', '']
    return '\n'.join(lines)


def main():

                    CG_ENTRY_SEEN_HITS=1, CG_TRAVERSAL_HITS=1, CG_EXHAUSTED_CALLS=3,
                    CG_NEW_VERTICES=6, CG_VERTICES_EXPANDED=6, CG_EDGES_EXAMINED=4,
                    CG_OWNER_SEARCHES=4)

    def test_complete_partitions_and_histograms(self):
        result = READER.derive(self.complete_metrics(), 'COMPLETE', 3, 2)
        self.assertTrue(all(x['result'] == 'PASS' for x in result['checks']))
        self.assertTrue(all(x['total_in_bucket_range'] for x in result['histograms'].values()))
        self.assertEqual(3 / 2, result['histograms']['C2_ACTUAL_LEAVES_']['mean_on_histogrammed_calls'])
        self.assertEqual(2, result['graph']['vertex_scan_volume_in_V_units'])

    def test_canceled_attempts_allow_missing_outcomes(self):
        result = READER.derive(dict(C2_QUERIES=1, C5_SCALAR_RESTRICT=1,
                                   C5_SCALAR_ORDINARY=1), 'TIMEOUT')
        partition = next(x for x in result['checks'] if x['name'] == 'C5 scalar terminal branch partition')
        self.assertEqual('GAP_ALLOWED_IN_PARTIAL_RUN', partition['result'])
        self.assertEqual(1, partition['gap'])
        self.assertFalse(any(x['result'] == 'REVIEW' for x in result['checks']))

    def test_complete_missing_outcome_needs_review(self):
        result = READER.derive(dict(C5_SCALAR_RESTRICT=1, C5_SCALAR_ORDINARY=1), 'COMPLETE')
        self.assertTrue(any(x['name'] == 'C5 scalar terminal branch partition' and
                            x['result'] == 'REVIEW' for x in result['checks']))

    def test_unterminated_live_END_line_is_ignored(self):
        line = b'BIDI_WORK_COUNTS run=1 phase=END status=COMPLETE diagnosticOnly=true C2_QUERIES=7'
        self.assertIsNone(READER.parse_log(line)['progress']['latest_counter_END'])
        complete = READER.parse_log(line + b'\n')
        self.assertEqual(1, complete['progress']['latest_counter_END'])
        self.assertEqual(7, complete['phases'][0]['metrics']['C2_QUERIES'])

    def test_progress_keeps_latest_complete_and_accepted(self):
        text = ('BIDI_RUN_START run=1 direction=FORWARD limit=1\n'
                'BIDI_RUN_END run=1 status=COMPLETE\n'
                'Run 1 (FORWARD) frontier: analysed 2, demand edges 4 in 2 method keys\n'
                'BIDI_WORK_COUNTS run=1 phase=END status=COMPLETE diagnosticOnly=true\n'
                'BIDI_RUN_START run=2 direction=BACKWARD limit=1\n'
                'BIDI_RUN_END run=2 status=TIMEOUT\n'
                'BIDI_WORK_COUNTS run=2 phase=END status=TIMEOUT diagnosticOnly=true C5_QUERIES=1\n'
                'BIDI_ANALYSIS_END run=2 status=TIMEOUT reason=ABNORMAL\n')
        result = READER.parse_log(text.encode())
        self.assertEqual(dict(latest_reached=2, latest_complete_engine=1,
                              latest_accepted_forward_frontier=1, latest_counter_END=2), result['progress'])
        self.assertEqual('TIMEOUT', result['analysis_end']['status'])

    def test_open_histogram_bucket_has_no_finite_upper_bound(self):
        h = READER.histogram({'C5_RAW_LEAVES_262144plus': 1}, 'C5_RAW_LEAVES_')
        self.assertEqual(262144, h['weighted_total_low'])
        self.assertIsNone(h['weighted_total_high'])
        self.assertEqual({'low': 262144, 'high': None}, h['quantile_buckets']['0.99'])

    def test_repeated_scratch_is_not_equated_to_repeated_tour(self):
        result = READER.derive(dict(CG_SCRATCH_CREATED=100,
                                   CG_UNIQUE_ROOTS_GRAPH_LIFETIME=1,
                                   CG_REPEATED_ROOT_SCRATCH=99), 'COMPLETE', 3, 2)
        self.assertEqual(0.99, result['graph']['repeated_root_scratch_fraction'])
        self.assertEqual(0, result['graph']['root_tour_repeats_lower_bound_single_graph'])

    def test_existing_query_counters_are_crosschecked_without_asserting_partial_balance(self):
        text = ('BIDI_RUN_START run=2 direction=BACKWARD limit=1\n'
                'BIDI_WORK_COUNTS run=2 phase=END status=TIMEOUT diagnosticOnly=true '
                'C2_QUERIES=3 C5_PAIR_OFFERS=5 C5_RESTRICT_CALLS=5 C5_BFS_STATES_ADMITTED=7 '
                'CG_C2_VISIBLE_VIEWS=2 CG_C5_VISIBLE_VIEWS=1\n'
                'BIDI_STATIC_CLOSURE_LOOKUP run=2 c2Direct=3 c5Candidates=5 c5Restrict=5 '
                'c5States=7 c2Visible=2 c5Visible=1\n')
        result = READER.parse_log(text.encode())
        self.assertEqual(6, len(result['phases'][0]['legacy_crosschecks']))
        self.assertTrue(all(x['result'] == 'PASS' for x in result['phases'][0]['legacy_crosschecks']))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

# Query-local owner visibility: source proof and measured lower bound

The run-2 counter snapshot stops on TIMEOUT. Latest reached is run-2; latest
complete and accepted is run-1. All source hashes match the frozen launch.

`Owners` has two construction sites in `FrozenStaticCompletion.Builder.build`:
one per bridge label and one per projected entry. The reported sizes are 14,449
and 1,965. Thus one frozen completion has at most 16,414 distinct Owners objects.
The objects hold private, immutable-by-ownership arrays and sets. No lookup
creates another Owners object. W/R attachments do not add another owner family.

Each visible View has exactly one lazy Reachability field. The current C5 path
creates and consumes the View within one query; the View does not escape to
another query. Only 20,621 C5 Views initialize reachability. They account for
1,697,456,250 completed reachesAny calls. The global started/outcome graph
partition is balanced in this snapshot, despite the partial engine.

```text
Distinct (View, Owners) pairs <= 20,621 * 16,414 = 338,473,094
Repeated calls >= 1,697,456,250 - 338,473,094 = 1,358,983,156
Repeated fraction >= 80.05998128%
```

The bound needs no retained per-query trace or pair-seen set. It is conservative:
different Owners objects may contain the same owner set, and many families may
never be touched by a particular View.

For the predicate's first completed call, preserve the existing evaluation.
There are two cases:

* True: either the fixed method belongs to outsideGraph, or an owner ID is in
  seen at return. Seen only grows. The same owner test on a later call returns
  true at its early seen test and changes neither seen nor pending. The outside
  shortcut also leaves an uninitialized lazy reachability field uninitialized.
* False: outsideGraph is false, no owner ID was reached, and pending is empty.
  Later predicates cannot grow seen from an empty pending queue. A later call
  with the same Owners again returns false without changing seen or pending.

Thus a completed boolean answer can be reused for the same Owners identity in
the same fixed-method View. Reuse preserves both the result and the current
reachability state, including with other owner queries between two identical
queries. A canceled evaluation must not be cached as a result. The current
empty-owner branch is included; the observed run has zero such calls.

The external finite source-model control checks A,B,A sequences on all 512
three-vertex directed graphs, including self edges, with four root choices
(including unknown), all eight owner subsets, and all outsideGraph shortcut
pairs. It passes 524,288 sequences and 1,572,864 result-and-state comparisons.
It uses canonical adjacency order. The general argument above does not depend
on that order. This is an executable source-model control, not a production
cache implementation or the complete formal model of a future change.

Current views are local to one lookup and already contain mutable scratch.
Keep any proposed memo in that same scope. This note does not establish safe
sharing across views, threads, methods or demand snapshots. It introduces no
global cache, weak cache, new fact label or new production storage.

An implementation would still need a cheap memo lookup for each outer request.
The lower bound is on original predicate-body calls that can be avoided, not
on CPU time or all work in the static loop. The prior fixed-entry pruning
candidate can remove some of the same requests, so their savings must not be
added. No optimization is implemented here.

See visibility-memo-proof.json for numeric inputs and source/model hashes.
